title: Re-Billing Amount When an Invoice Still Billed the Former Dental Tier (Premium Billing Accounts)
content:
**Rule.** On Premium Billing Accounts, a re-billing amount is added to the dental tier-difference credit when Cascade issued an invoice that still billed the dropped tier. It is added after any deduction and after the floor at 0.00; the credit is rounded half up to the cent once, at the end.

| Invoice issued last | Days from the departed dependent's termination date to that invoice's issue date | Amount added |
|---|---|---|
| billed the tier before the drop | 60 or more | 25.00 |
| billed the tier before the drop | 1 to 59 | 10.00 |
| any other case | | nothing |

**Reading the invoice issued last.** The invoice issued last is the one issued on the latest date (of two issued on the same day, the one recorded first). It is read against the plans it could bill. Its premium is its months covered multiplied by the total of the monthly premiums of the plans priced, reduced by the prepay discount percentage (4 percent on Cascade Individual Annual Prepay, 0 percent elsewhere) and rounded half up to the cent. The plans priced are:
- the subscriber's Dental PPO Plans plan (the subscriber's active enrollment funded by the account with the latest coverage effective date, the one recorded first on a tie);
- each Orthodontic Benefit Riders rider the account funds that is active or applied, at its rider plan's monthly premium per covered person, riders applied for after the invoice's date being left out;
- the subscriber's Prepaid Dental HMO Plans enrollment funded by the account that is applied or active (neither terminated nor cancelled) (the one with the latest coverage effective date, the one recorded first on a tie), at its recorded tier, when it was applied for on or before the invoice's date;
- the subscriber's Vision Plans enrollment funded by the account that is applied or active (neither terminated nor cancelled) (the one with the latest coverage effective date, the one recorded first on a tie), at its recorded tier, when it was applied for on or before the invoice's date.

The invoice billed the tier before the drop when its amount equals, to the cent, that premium with the dental plan priced at the tier billed before the drop — with or without the ended orthodontic rider (the account's terminated rider with the latest termination date, the one recorded first on a tie) priced in at its rider plan's monthly premium per covered person.

**Where the reading is made.** Only on an account on which, for each orthodontic rider plan, its active riders and, separately, its applied riders were either all applied for on or before the invoice's date or all applied for on one date, so that the records show which riders were applied for after that date (when that one date is later, those riders). On any other account the invoice is not taken to have billed the tier before the drop and no re-billing amount is added.

**The departed dependent and the tier before the drop.** The subscriber's child, spouse or domestic partner whose dental enrollment funded by the account ended for loss of eligibility, the one with the latest termination date (of two with the same date, a child's before a spouse's or domestic partner's, and of two of one relationship the one recorded first); the tier before the drop is the coverage tier recorded on that enrollment.

**Hypothetical case.** Monthly invoice issued 12 August, 75 days after a dependent's termination on 29 May, for 1 month at 121.30. Priced plans: dental at the former tier 96.40, one active rider at 24.90, no DHMO, no vision: 121.30, equal to the cent — 25.00 is added. Had the invoice been issued 40 days after, 10.00.
